# Second-scale affine floor motions: actual neutral paths and the collar penalty

This checks a proposed new mechanism at the selected minima: move a nearly zero supporting facet at its exponentially small height while lifting or lowering the affine parameter. The first-order tests of signed normal-affine motions are already in the common physical cone. A fully co-moving continuous translation is an exact admissible neutral path, preserving critical caps and the entire optimization problem. The singular logarithmic second-order term in a flat collar is positive, rather than a universal source of descent.

This does not classify arbitrary second-order shape deformations. In particular it supplies neither a new OC proof nor a theorem saying that every localized collar deformation is redundant.

## 1. The exact prelimit identities already include exponential scales

At a sufficiently small selected minimum, use the proved complete common separator from `candidate 9158d8d941246660`. Its physical cone includes every admissible continuous-normal field which is finite convex in physical position. In particular, for any continuous normal function `psi_j` and affine physical function `ell_j`, both signs of

    Phi_j(n,w)=psi_j(n) ell_j(w)

are admissible: each is affine in `w`. There is no requirement that the coefficients, angular localization, or size be uniform as `j` varies. They only have to be finite at that particular selected minimum. The SAME dual therefore obeys the exact equality

    int Xi_j(n,w) psi_j(n) ell_j(w) d eta_j(n,w)=0.                (1)

Here `Xi_j` is the complete physical density, not just `W_j-beta_j+lambda_j ell_{j,+}`. All energy, covariance, and normalization terms remain in it.

The affine parameter directions also admit both signs. Writing the actual inverse contact rows in their normalized form, their exact equality is

    sum_i (sigma_ij/L_ij) h_j(Y_ij)
        = (1/M_j) int h_j/L_j dm_j                 (2)

for every affine `h_j`. In particular `h_j` can be of size `eta_j=exp(-R/lambda_j)`, or its reciprocal, for any fixed finite `j`. Such a choice merely rescales an already valid affine identity.

Consequently coupling a signed normal-affine body speed with an affine parameter lift of exponential size yields no additional first-order stationarity equation. A shrinking angular window is also already allowed in (1). Passing it to a limit may reveal a useful consequence, but requires control of the other boundary mass in that window; it cannot be declared a new normal-conditional equality without that control.

Likewise the nonnegative collar potential

    psi_j(n) [t_j-A_j(w)]_+,   psi_j>=0,

is already a convex physical test whenever `A_j` is an affine majorant. Its possibly exponential threshold does not enlarge the cone. Its negative generally is not convex, so the available inequality cannot be replaced by an equality merely because its support is thin.

This statement does not assert that arbitrary independent facet speeds on individual integer fibers are admissible. The physical affine function must be defined on the whole mixed space, and the complete body path from the applicability theorem must still be used.

## 2. An actual co-moving path preserves criticality exactly

There is an exact neutral family through every selected configuration, at every exponential scale. Fix a continuous vector `v` and any positive scalar `eta_j`. For real `t` near zero, put

    T_j,t(z,X)=(z,X+t eta_j v),
    C_j,t=T_j,t C_j,
    L_j,t(z,X)=L_j(z,X-t eta_j v).

Translate every source mark by the same map. Translate a cap `{a.z+u.X>=b}` to `{a.z+u.X>=b+t eta_j u.v}`. This is a bijection of the entire family of ambient halfspaces, preserves `Z^n x R^d`, has determinant one in each fiber, and preserves the exact fiber measures.

All cap masses and halfspace depths are unchanged. Every formerly critical cap remains critical for the translated source. The log normalization is unchanged by the change of variables. The within-fiber covariance, the intrinsic source energy, and the buffered value are translation invariant, so the selected regularized objective, its scale parameter, and its source/cap compatibility remain exactly unchanged. This is an actual path of the whole problem, not a formal independent perturbation of its arrays.

For one affine component `A_j=a_j+c_j.X`, the translated parameter is `A_j-t eta_j c_j.v`. Thus a boundary displacement in its positive coordinate and the opposite parameter lift preserve the parameter's boundary value. This realizes the co-moving-floor mode as a genuine neutral motion when the entire body and the cap/source data move together.

A local motion of only one facet need not be such a translation; its remaining global effects require a separate calculation. The exponential scale alone does not break this neutral symmetry.

## 3. Exact finite-amplitude logarithmic remainder in a flat collar

The following is an algebraic local calculation, not an assertion that a frozen dual functional equals the reoptimized objective to second order. Use a physical affine coordinate `x` whose current collar floor is `x=0`, with parameter `L=eta+x` and constant transverse area `A>0`. Take a fixed upper endpoint `T>0`. Move the lower boundary to `h=eta s` and lift the parameter by `k=eta t`, where `1+s+t>0`. Its raw logarithmic contribution is

    I(h,k)=A int_h^T log(eta+x+k) dx.

Let `F(y)=y log y-y` for `y>0`. Then exactly

    I(h,k)=A[F(T+eta+k)-F(eta+h+k)].

The current first derivatives are

    I_h(0,0)=-A log eta,
    I_k(0,0)=A log((T+eta)/eta).

Define the nonnegative convex function

    J(v)=(1+v)log(1+v)-v,  v>-1.

Subtracting the complete first-order Taylor term gives the exact identity

    I(eta s,eta t)-I(0,0)-eta s I_h(0,0)-eta t I_k(0,0)
      = A B_F(T+eta+eta t,T+eta) - A eta J(s+t),                 (3)

where `B_F(y,x)=F(y)-F(x)-F'(x)(y-x)>=0` is the upper-endpoint Bregman remainder. For bounded `s,t` and `eta` tending to zero, that upper remainder is `O(eta^2/T)`.

The singular physical logarithmic term has coefficient `-lambda`, so its nonlinear collar contribution is

    +lambda A eta J(s+t)
        -lambda A B_F(T+eta+eta t,T+eta).                         (4)

The singular part is nonnegative and depends only on the sum of the boundary displacement and parameter lift. Its infinitesimal Hessian is

    (lambda A/eta) [[1,1],[1,1]],

which is positive semidefinite of rank one. The null direction is exactly `t=-s`, the co-moving-floor direction. If the collar area is of order `lambda`, as in a finite nonzero logarithmic surface defect, the leading positive remainder has scale `lambda^2 eta`, while the regular upper-endpoint term is smaller by the exponential factor `eta/lambda`.

At the null direction the singular term vanishes; the remaining smooth body, source, covariance, quantile, and normalization terms must all be retained. Their signs are not determined by (3). In particular the negative upper-endpoint term alone is not a proof of an actual descent.

## 4. What this closes, and what remains genuinely new

The suggested first-order family of signed normal-affine facet motions, affine floor lifts, and positive-part affine collar tests is already in the audited physical/parameter cone. Exponential coefficients do not evade that fact. A complete co-moving translation is exactly neutral while preserving all criticality and normalization data. Changing the floor instead has a positive singular logarithmic penalty in the exact flat-collar calculation.

A genuinely new second-scale route would therefore have to control the residual global shape response along a co-moving null mode, including changes of optimal source marks, cap quantiles, active support allocations, covariance, and energy. The currently proved first-order envelope does not supply that second-order control. No additional complementarity or pointwise equality `W+r=beta` has been inferred here.
